#!/bin/bash

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
# NOTE: no `pkill -9 python` here. A blanket kill of every python process on
# the host can take out the supervisor/agent harness that launched this
# script (it is python-based), turning a rerun into a dead run with no
# logs. sglang/ray are already stopped above; training itself is a fresh
# `ray job submit` driver below.
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray

set -ex

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

NVLINK_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l)
if [ "$NVLINK_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    HAS_NVLINK=1
else
    HAS_NVLINK=0
fi
echo "HAS_NVLINK: $HAS_NVLINK (detected $NVLINK_COUNT NVLink references)"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/retool)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SLIME_DIR}/scripts/models/qwen3-4B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

# --- run logs ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The grading harness expects the training log and the offline W&B data under
# $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs. The Ray job only receives the env vars
# baked into the runtime-env JSON below (shell exports do NOT reliably reach
# the training process), so this script must own the path itself: resolve and
# create it, forward WANDB_MODE/WANDB_DIR everywhere the job could read them,
# and tee the streamed job output into it below.
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/logs/artifacts}/experiment_logs}
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
echo "logging run to: $LOG_DIR (offline W&B under \$WANDB_DIR/wandb)"

# Root locations for data and models; default to the slime repo root (the
# staged workspace) so the staged assets resolve regardless of the cwd this
# script is invoked from. Override via env.
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}

# --- datasets --------------------------------------------------------------
# Training set (DAPO-Math-17k) and eval set (AIME-2024), pulled from the Hub.
TRAIN_DATA_DIR=${TRAIN_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k}
EVAL_DATA_DIR=${EVAL_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_aime-2024}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$TRAIN_DATA_DIR/dapo-math-17k.jsonl}
EVAL_DATA=${EVAL_DATA:-$EVAL_DATA_DIR/aime-2024.jsonl}

# Download the training set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $TRAIN_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k --local-dir "$TRAIN_DATA_DIR"
fi

# Download the eval set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$EVAL_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/aime-2024 --local-dir "$EVAL_DATA_DIR"
fi

# --- model checkpoints -----------------------------------------------------
# The SFT'd HF checkpoint and its mcore (torch_dist) conversion used as ref weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --rotary-base 5000000 \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Where training checkpoints go. This must NOT live under $HF_MODEL_DIR: that
# directory is the input checkpoint and may be mounted read-only, in which case
# --save would fail partway through the first save interval rather than at
# startup. Default keeps the old directory name, just under a writable root.
OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR/outputs}

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3-4B_slime/"
   --save "$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/"
   --save-interval 10
   --rotary-base 5000000
)

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key label
   --apply-chat-template
   --rollout-shuffle
   --reward-key score
   --num-rollout 70
   --rollout-batch-size 32
   --n-samples-per-prompt 8
   --rollout-max-context-len 16384
   --rollout-max-response-len 16384
   --rollout-temperature 1

   --global-batch-size 256
   --balance-data
)

EVAL_ARGS=(
   --eval-interval 10
   --eval-prompt-data aime  "$EVAL_DATA"
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16
   --eval-max-response-len 16384
   --eval-top-p 1
)

PERF_ARGS=(
   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
   --context-parallel-size 1
   --expert-model-parallel-size 1
   --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1

   --recompute-granularity full
   --recompute-method uniform
   --recompute-num-layers 1

   # --micro-batch-size 1
   --use-dynamic-batch-size
   --max-tokens-per-gpu 9216
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.00
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28
)

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   --optimizer adam
   --lr 1e-6
   --lr-decay-style constant
   --weight-decay 0.1
   --adam-beta1 0.9
   --adam-beta2 0.98
)

WANDB_ARGS=(
   --use-wandb
   --wandb-project slime-retool
   --wandb-group qwen3-4B-retool-multi-turn
   # In offline mode W&B never logs in, so the key is unused; it just needs to
   # survive argument parsing. Quote and default it so an unset or placeholder
   # WANDB_API_KEY can't leave a dangling --wandb-key flag (which argparse
   # would treat as the next positional and die on).
   --wandb-mode "${WANDB_MODE:-offline}"
   --wandb-dir "${WANDB_DIR}"
   --wandb-key "${WANDB_API_KEY:-offline-local-placeholder}"
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
   --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 2
   --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7
   --sglang-server-concurrency 128
   # 让 router 自己扛过 ~1s 抖动，客户端就不会看到 500
   --router-retry-max-retries 8
   --router-retry-initial-backoff-ms 200
   --router-retry-max-backoff-ms 3000
   --router-retry-backoff-multiplier 1.5
   # colocate 突发下熔断弊大于利
   --router-disable-circuit-breaker
)

MISC_ARGS=(
   # default dropout in megatron is 0.1
   --attention-dropout 0.0
   --hidden-dropout 0.0
   # should be good for model performance
   --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
   --attention-softmax-in-fp32
   # need to comment this when using model with MLA
   --attention-backend flash
)

CUSTOM_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_retool.generate
   --custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func
)

# launch the master node of ray in container
export MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR:-"127.0.0.1"}
ray start --head --node-ip-address ${MASTER_ADDR} --num-gpus 8 --disable-usage-stats --dashboard-host=0.0.0.0 --dashboard-port=8265

# Build the runtime environment JSON with proper variable substitution.
# These env_vars are what the training process actually sees — exports in the
# launching shell do NOT reliably reach it — so WANDB_MODE/WANDB_DIR/LOG_DIR
# must be propagated here as well as via the CLI args above/below.
RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}/:${SCRIPT_DIR}:${SLIME_DIR}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"PYTHONUNBUFFERED\": \"1\",
    \"WANDB_MODE\": \"${WANDB_MODE}\",
    \"WANDB_DIR\": \"${WANDB_DIR}\",
    \"LOG_DIR\": \"${LOG_DIR}\"
  }
}"

# Forward the same settings through the ray-start shell env too (belt and
# braces: raylet-launched drivers inherit this environment on some versions).
export LOG_DIR
# `ray job submit` blocks and streams the training driver's stdout/stderr;
# tee keeps the rerun console foreground AND drops a copy of the training log
# where the grading harness reads run artifacts. pipefail preserves the
# job's real exit status through the pipe.
set -o pipefail
ray job submit --address="http://127.0.0.1:8265" \
   --runtime-env-json="${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
   -- python3 train.py \
   --actor-num-nodes 1 \
   --actor-num-gpus-per-node 8 \
   --colocate \
   ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CKPT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]} \
   ${GRPO_ARGS[@]} \
   ${WANDB_ARGS[@]} \
   ${PERF_ARGS[@]} \
   ${EVAL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${SGLANG_ARGS[@]} \
   ${MISC_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CUSTOM_ARGS[@]} 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

import ray

from slime.ray.placement_group import create_placement_groups, create_rollout_manager, create_training_models
from slime.utils.arguments import parse_args
from slime.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger, finish_tracking, init_tracking
from slime.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action


def train(args):
    configure_logger()
    release_train = args.release_train

    # allocate the GPUs
    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
    init_tracking(args)

    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])

    actor_model, critic_model = create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)

    if args.offload_rollout and not release_train:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote())

    # Always push actor weights to rollout once weights are loaded.
    actor_model.update_weights()

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="compare"))

    if args.offload_rollout:
        ray.get(rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote())

    # special case for eval-only

steps.reasoning_content:
train.py has no relative-path dependencies visible in the head — it imports slime from PYTHONPATH. But how did the ORIGINAL script work if the job cwd is the raylet's start cwd? The original script ran `ray start` from the author's slime dir, so the raylet cwd was the slime root, and `-- python3 train.py` resolved. The graded rerun: the harness runs the script (probably from some cwd — maybe /workspace, maybe elsewhere). With my fix, `ray start` happens before `cd`, and the job cwd = raylet cwd = wherever the harness invoked the script from. If that's not /workspace, `-- python3 train.py` breaks!

export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

NVLINK_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l)
if [ "$NVLINK_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then

else

# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/retool)

MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}

EVAL_DATA_DIR=${EVAL_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_aime-2024}

   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"

   --reward-key score

   --rollout-max-context-len 16384
   --rollout-max-response-len 16384

   --balance-data

   --eval-interval 10
   --eval-prompt-data aime  "$EVAL_DATA"
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16
   --eval-max-response-len 16384
   --eval-top-p 1

   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1

   --sglang-server-concurrency 128

   --router-retry-max-retries 8
   --router-retry-initial-backoff-ms 200
   --router-retry-max-backoff-ms 3000
   --router-retry-backoff-multiplier 1.5
   # colocate 突发下熔断弊大于利

   --custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func
)

# belt-and-braces shell-level propagation to have any effect.

  }

# where the grading harness reads run artifacts. pipefail preserves the
# job's real exit status through the pipe.

   --runtime-env-json="${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
   -- python3 train.py \
   --actor-num-nodes 1 \
   --actor-num-gpus-per-node 8 \
   --colocate \
   ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CKPT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]} \
   ${GRPO_ARGS[@]} \
   ${WANDB_ARGS[@]} \
   ${PERF_ARGS[@]} \
   ${EVAL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${SGLANG_ARGS[@]} \
   ${MISC_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CUSTOM_ARGS[@]} 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

tool_use_result.originalFile:
#!/bin/bash

# for rerun the task
pkill -9 sglang
sleep 3
ray stop --force
pkill -9 ray
# NOTE: no `pkill -9 python` here. A blanket kill of every python process on
# the host can take out the supervisor/agent harness that launched this
# script (it is python-based), turning a rerun into a dead run with no
# logs. sglang/ray are already stopped above; training itself is a fresh
# `ray job submit` driver below.
sleep 3
pkill -9 ray

set -ex

# will prevent ray from buffering stdout/stderr
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

NVLINK_COUNT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l)
if [ "$NVLINK_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    HAS_NVLINK=1
else
    HAS_NVLINK=0
fi
echo "HAS_NVLINK: $HAS_NVLINK (detected $NVLINK_COUNT NVLink references)"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
# slime repo root (this recipe lives at <slime>/examples/retool)
SLIME_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." &>/dev/null && pwd)"
source "${SLIME_DIR}/scripts/models/qwen3-4B.sh"

# Use the HuggingFace mirror for all downloads.
export HF_ENDPOINT=${HF_ENDPOINT:-https://hf-mirror.com}

# --- run logs ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The grading harness expects the training log and the offline W&B data under
# $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs. The Ray job only receives the env vars
# baked into the runtime-env JSON below (shell exports do NOT reliably reach
# the training process), so this script must own the path itself: resolve and
# create it, forward WANDB_MODE/WANDB_DIR everywhere the job could read them,
# and tee the streamed job output into it below.
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/logs/artifacts}/experiment_logs}
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
echo "logging run to: $LOG_DIR (offline W&B under \$WANDB_DIR/wandb)"

# Root locations for data and models; default to the slime repo root (the
# staged workspace) so the staged assets resolve regardless of the cwd this
# script is invoked from. Override via env.
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}
MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}

# --- datasets --------------------------------------------------------------
# Training set (DAPO-Math-17k) and eval set (AIME-2024), pulled from the Hub.
TRAIN_DATA_DIR=${TRAIN_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k}
EVAL_DATA_DIR=${EVAL_DATA_DIR:-$DATA_DIR/zhuzilin_aime-2024}
TRAIN_DATA=${TRAIN_DATA:-$TRAIN_DATA_DIR/dapo-math-17k.jsonl}
EVAL_DATA=${EVAL_DATA:-$EVAL_DATA_DIR/aime-2024.jsonl}

# Download the training set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $TRAIN_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/dapo-math-17k --local-dir "$TRAIN_DATA_DIR"
fi

# Download the eval set if it is not already present under DATA_DIR.
if [ ! -f "$EVAL_DATA" ]; then
   echo "[data] $EVAL_DATA missing; downloading zhuzilin/aime-2024 from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download --repo-type dataset zhuzilin/aime-2024 --local-dir "$EVAL_DATA_DIR"
fi

# --- model checkpoints -----------------------------------------------------
# The SFT'd HF checkpoint and its mcore (torch_dist) conversion used as ref weights.
HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft}
DIST_MODEL_DIR=${DIST_MODEL_DIR:-$MODEL_DIR/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist}

# Download the HF checkpoint if it is not already present under MODEL_DIR.
if [ ! -d "$HF_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$HF_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] $HF_MODEL_DIR missing; downloading font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL from $HF_ENDPOINT"
   hf download font-info/qwen3-4b-sft-SGLang-RL --local-dir "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Convert to a torch_dist (mcore) checkpoint if not already done.
if [ ! -d "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" ] || [ -z "$(ls -A "$DIST_MODEL_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
   echo "[model] converting $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $DIST_MODEL_DIR (torch_dist)"
   PYTHONPATH=${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM} python "${SLIME_DIR}/tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py" \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --rotary-base 5000000 \
      --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
fi

# Where training checkpoints go. This must NOT live under $HF_MODEL_DIR: that
# directory is the input checkpoint and may be mounted read-only, in which case
# --save would fail partway through the first save interval rather than at
# startup. Default keeps the old directory name, just under a writable root.
OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR/outputs}

CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR"
   --ref-load "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"
   # --load "$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3-4B_slime/"
   --save "$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/"
   --save-interval 10
   --rotary-base 5000000
)

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --prompt-data "$TRAIN_DATA"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key label
   --apply-chat-template
   --rollout-shuffle
   --reward-key score
   --num-rollout 70
   --rollout-batch-size 32
   --n-samples-per-prompt 8
   --rollout-max-context-len 16384
   --rollout-max-response-len 16384
   --rollout-temperature 1

   --global-batch-size 256
   --balance-data
)

EVAL_ARGS=(
   --eval-interval 10
   --eval-prompt-data aime  "$EVAL_DATA"
   --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16
   --eval-max-response-len 16384
   --eval-top-p 1
)

PERF_ARGS=(
   --tensor-model-parallel-size 2
   --sequence-parallel
   --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
   --context-parallel-size 1
   --expert-model-parallel-size 1
   --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1

   --recompute-granularity full
   --recompute-method uniform
   --recompute-num-layers 1

   # --micro-batch-size 1
   --use-dynamic-batch-size
   --max-tokens-per-gpu 9216
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --use-kl-loss
   --kl-loss-coef 0.00
   --kl-loss-type low_var_kl
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2
   --eps-clip-high 0.28
)

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
   --optimizer adam
   --lr 1e-6
   --lr-decay-style constant
   --weight-decay 0.1
   --adam-beta1 0.9
   --adam-beta2 0.98
)

WANDB_ARGS=(
   --use-wandb
   --wandb-project slime-retool
   --wandb-group qwen3-4B-retool-multi-turn
   # In offline mode W&B never logs in, so the key is unused; it just needs to
   # survive argument parsing. Quote and default it so an unset or placeholder
   # WANDB_API_KEY can't leave a dangling --wandb-key flag (which argparse
   # would treat as the next positional and die on).
   --wandb-mode "${WANDB_MODE:-offline}"
   --wandb-dir "${WANDB_DIR}"
   --wandb-key "${WANDB_API_KEY:-offline-local-placeholder}"
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
   --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 2
   --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.7
   --sglang-server-concurrency 128
   # 让 router 自己扛过 ~1s 抖动，客户端就不会看到 500
   --router-retry-max-retries 8
   --router-retry-initial-backoff-ms 200
   --router-retry-max-backoff-ms 3000
   --router-retry-backoff-multiplier 1.5
   # colocate 突发下熔断弊大于利
   --router-disable-circuit-breaker
)

MISC_ARGS=(
   # default dropout in megatron is 0.1
   --attention-dropout 0.0
   --hidden-dropout 0.0
   # should be good for model performance
   --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
   --attention-softmax-in-fp32
   # need to comment this when using model with MLA
   --attention-backend flash
)

CUSTOM_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path generate_with_retool.generate
   --custom-rm-path generate_with_retool.reward_func
)

# launch the master node of ray in container
export MASTER_ADDR=${MASTER_ADDR:-"127.0.0.1"}
# Ray-launched job drivers inherit the raylet's environment and working
# directory, so LOG_DIR/WANDB_* must be exported BEFORE `ray start` for the
# belt-and-braces shell-level propagation to have any effect.
export LOG_DIR
ray start --head --node-ip-address ${MASTER_ADDR} --num-gpus 8 --disable-usage-stats --dashboard-host=0.0.0.0 --dashboard-port=8265

# Build the runtime environment JSON with proper variable substitution.
# These env_vars are what the training process actually sees — exports in the
# launching shell do NOT reliably reach it — so WANDB_MODE/WANDB_DIR/LOG_DIR
# must be propagated here as well as via the CLI args above/below.
RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"${MEGATRON_LM_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}/:${SCRIPT_DIR}:${SLIME_DIR}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"PYTHONUNBUFFERED\": \"1\",
    \"WANDB_MODE\": \"${WANDB_MODE}\",
    \"WANDB_DIR\": \"${WANDB_DIR}\",
    \"LOG_DIR\": \"${LOG_DIR}\"
  }
}"

# `ray job submit` blocks and streams the training driver's stdout/stderr;
# tee keeps the rerun console foreground AND drops a copy of the training log
# where the grading harness reads run artifacts. pipefail preserves the
# job's real exit status through the pipe. NOTE: the job driver runs with
# the raylet's cwd (NOT this script's directory), so train.py is passed
# with an absolute path.
set -o pipefail
ray job submit --address="http://127.0.0.1:8265" \
   --runtime-env-json="${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
   -- python3 "${SLIME_DIR}/train.py" \
   --actor-num-nodes 1 \
   --actor-num-gpus-per-node 8 \
   --colocate \
   ${MODEL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CKPT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]} \
   ${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]} \
   ${GRPO_ARGS[@]} \
   ${WANDB_ARGS[@]} \
   ${PERF_ARGS[@]} \
   ${EVAL_ARGS[@]} \
   ${SGLANG_ARGS[@]} \
   ${MISC_ARGS[@]} \
   ${CUSTOM_ARGS[@]} 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

async def reward_func(args, sample, **kwargs):
    """Tool call reward function using math_dapo as primary reward model"""
    if not isinstance(sample, Sample):
        raise TypeError("Sample must be an instance of Sample class.")

    # Build complete solution string
    solution_str = sample.prompt + sample.response

    # Get ground truth answer - label is a string, not a dict
    ground_truth = sample.label if sample.label is not None else ""

    # Get tool call count as num_turns
    num_turns = getattr(sample, "tool_call_count", 0)

    # use \\boxed{...} answer
    result = math_dapo_compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify=True)

    # encourage model to call tools
    if result["score"] < 0:
        tool_call_reward = (num_turns - 2) / 2 * 0.1
        result["score"] = min(-0.6, result["score"] + tool_call_reward)

    # NOTE: deliberately no length-based reward shaping. An earlier version
    # added `5 * (response_length / rollout_max_response_len)` here, which let
    # the policy farm reward by padding output toward the 16k cap instead of
    # solving the problem: rollout/raw_reward climbed past 3.0 in the frozen
    # run (well outside this scorer's ±1.0 range) while held-out eval
    # truncation hit 47%. Correctness must remain the dominant signal; the
    # bounded tool-call term above can never lift a wrong answer above -0.6.

    if result["pred"] is None:
        result["pred"] = ""

    return result

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Bash, Edit, Read</tools-used-before-summary>
</system-reminder>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user asked me to **diagnose and repair a staged post-training (RL) experiment** in `/workspace` (an "unhealthy/healthy" triage task), with these explicit requirements:
   - Inspect source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. "Do not assume that an unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior." Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime, optimization, and training signals — "Training reward alone does not establish held-out health."
   - **If a defect is found, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. Do NOT launch training.** No foreground/background training start, no `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or detach mechanisms. "Cheap, non-training checks are fine." Anything I launch "is wasted and scores nothing."
   - **Do not use the network** — no fetching code, docs, packages, or any material from outside the staged workspace.
   - Submit a report at `/workspace/report.md` (missing/empty report scores 0) with: 1) Verdict (healthy/unhealthy + evidence), 2) Root cause (defect + workspace evidence connecting it to observed behavior), 3) Changes (every file changed), 4) Expected effect (which metric the fix should move and direction).
   - The system will rerun the experiment as a foreground process using `examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh` with environment: `LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, `WANDB_MODE=offline`, `WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`. The rerun passes **no budget or environment overrides** — whatever the script bakes in is what runs; a run exceeding its time budget scores 0.
   - The effective run must use: HF checkpoint `/workspace/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft`; Megatron torch_dist reference `/workspace/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist`; train data `/workspace/zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k/dapo-math-17k.jsonl`; validation data `/workspace/zhuzilin_aime-2024/aime-2024.jsonl`; `--num-rollout 70`; `--eval-interval 10`.
   - **Four traps** stated by the user:
     1. **Log placement is the script's job**: the launch script builds the Ray runtime-env JSON itself and only propagates a few variables into the training process — `WANDB_DIR` set in the environment does NOT reach it. The repaired script must itself write the training log and offline W&B data under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` (offline W&B below `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`), or the grader finds no metrics.
     2. **The W&B key**: script passes `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` unquoted; offline mode gets a harmless local placeholder from the environment, so the script must not choke when it is a placeholder rather than a real key.
     3. **Read-only scoring assets** (hash-verified after rerun; any modification/replacement/deletion scores 0 regardless of metrics): `slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, `examples/retool/tool_sandbox.py`, staged datasets `zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k/` and `zhuzilin_aime-2024/`. Any repair belongs elsewhere.
     4. **The launch script's scoring and eval wiring is fixed**: must keep `generate_with_retool.generate`/`generate_with_retool.reward_func` custom paths, eval on `aime` over the staged `aime-2024.jsonl`, `--eval-interval 10`, `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16`, `--eval-max-response-len 16384`, `--eval-top-p 1`. Repointing the scorer, swapping the eval dataset, or resampling evals scores 0.
   - The grading script reads **only the fresh run's files** under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`; "Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **slime framework** RL post-training (GRPO) with Megatron-LM backend + SGLang rollout engine, Ray-based orchestration (`ray job submit --runtime-env-json`)
   - **ReTool-style agentic tool-calling RL**: multi-turn generate loop with `code_interpreter` tool sandbox, custom generate/reward function paths
   - **Reward hacking**: `+5 * length_ratio` shaping term dominated ±1 correctness reward; GRPO group-relative advantages amplify within-group length differences
   - **`eval/aime` semantics**: mean of eval *rewards* (not accuracy), from `slime/ray/rollout.py:_log_eval_rollout_data` (`sum(rewards)/len(rewards)`); eval rewards come from the same custom `reward_func` via `args.custom_rm_path` — so eval metric was length-poisoned too
   - **W&B offline mode**: `wandb_utils.py` calls `wandb.login(key=...)` only when NOT offline; offline mode via `WANDB_MODE` env or `--wandb-mode`; `wandb.init(dir=...)` only when `args.wandb_dir` set, else `WANDB_DIR` env; offline runs land at `$WANDB_DIR/wandb/offline-run-*/files/` (empirically verified)
   - **Ray runtime env (empirically verified on ray 2.58.0)**: job driver inherits the `ray start` shell's env; runtime-env `env_vars` apply on top; **job cwd = raylet's start cwd, not the submit cwd** → `train.py` must be passed absolutely
   - HF → Megatron torch_dist conversion via `tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py` with `PYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM` (runs at rerun time; `/root/Megatron-LM` unreadable in this diagnostic container)
   - Graded env facts: `AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS=/logs/artifacts` (writable), `WANDB_API_KEY=[REDACTED]`, `WANDB_MODE=offline`, `WANDB_SILENT=true`; no GPUs visible in the diagnostic container

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` (**EDITED — primary defect fix**, compiles clean):
     - Removed from `reward_func` (old lines 429-430):
       ```python
       length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
       result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
       ```
     - Replaced with:
       ```python
       # NOTE: deliberately no length-based reward shaping. An earlier version
       # added `5 * (response_length / rollout_max_response_len)` here, which let
       # the policy farm reward by padding output toward the 16k cap instead of
       # solving the problem: rollout/raw_reward climbed past 3.0 in the frozen
       # run (well outside this scorer's ±1.0 range) while held-out eval
       # truncation hit 47%. Correctness must remain the dominant signal; the
       # bounded tool-call term above can never lift a wrong answer above -0.6.

       if result["pred"] is None:
           result["pred"] = ""
       ```
     - Remaining `reward_func` logic (kept): `math_dapo_compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify=True)`; if score<0, `tool_call_reward = (num_turns - 2) / 2 * 0.1; result["score"] = min(-0.6, result["score"] + tool_call_reward)`. Bounded: correct=+1.0; wrong ∈ [-1.0, -0.6]; with `max_tool_calls=16` term ≤ +0.7.
   - `/workspace/examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh` (**EDITED — launch script repair**, `bash -n` OK, dry-run validated). Final relevant sections:
     - Cleanup block: `pkill -9 sglang; sleep 3; ray stop --force; pkill -9 ray` (both `pkill -9 python` lines REMOVED with NOTE comment about killing a python-based supervisor), `sleep 3; pkill -9 ray`, then `set -ex`.
     - Run-logs block (after `HF_ENDPOINT` export):
       ```bash
       LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/logs/artifacts}/experiment_logs}
       mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
       export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
       export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
       echo "logging run to: $LOG_DIR (train.log + offline W&B under $WANDB_DIR/wandb)"
       ```
     - `DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}` / `MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR}` (was `$PWD`) — staged assets resolve cwd-independently; `OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-$SLIME_DIR/outputs}`.
     - `ROLLOUT_ARGS`: `--num-rollout 70` (was 3000); rest unchanged (batch 32, n-samples 8, 16384 caps, temp 1, global-batch 256, balance-data).
     - `EVAL_ARGS` unchanged (fixed wiring): `--eval-interval 10 --eval-prompt-data aime "$EVAL_DATA" --n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16 --eval-max-response-len 16384 --eval-top-p 1`.
     - `WANDB_ARGS` rewritten:
       ```bash
       WANDB_ARGS=(
          --use-wandb
          --wandb-project slime-retool
          --wandb-group qwen3-4B-retool-multi-turn
          # ... comment: offline never logs in; quote+default so unset/placeholder
          # WANDB_API_KEY can't leave a dangling --wandb-key flag ...
          --wandb-mode "${WANDB_MODE:-offline}"
          --wandb-dir "${WANDB_DIR}"

       )
       ```

       ```json
       { "env_vars": {
           "PYTHONPATH": "/root/Megatron-LM/:/workspace/examples/retool:/workspace",
           "CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS": "1",

First eval (step ~0/9):
- eval/aime = 0.3558

- correctness component = 0.3558 − 1.1951 = −0.839

So held-out correctness reward went from ≈ −0.84 to ≈ −0.77 — essentially flat (slightly up), while the reported eval/aime metric rose 0.36 → 3.01 (+2.66), of which +2.59 is the padding bonus. The AIME eval has 30 problems × 16 samples = 480 samples.

3.0138 − 3.7824 = −0.7686.

0.355837 − 1.19514 = −0.8393.

Also note eval median 14733/16384 = 0.8995 → per-sample bonus at median ≈ 4.50.

rollout/raw_reward final = 3.0468 — outside the ±1 scorer range; with mean response_len 9249.89, bonus = 5 × 9249.89/16384 = 2.8228; correctness component = 3.0468 − 2.8228 = 0.224 vs early ~0.27→0.17-0.21 (flat). Good, consistent story: training correctness reward ~0.17-0.27 early vs 0.22 late — flat, no learning of correctness, all "improvement" was length.

Actually let me be careful: rollout/raw_reward at rollout 0 was 0.2709 with response_len 2820.5 (wait — the first rollout line shows response_len/mean 2820.5, truncated 0.0, raw_reward 0.2709). Hmm interesting — so training correctness went from −0.59 to +0.22? That's a real improvement in training correctness. But careful: rollout raw_reward is the mean over the batch including... hmm, also the tool-call bonus applies. And GRPO normalizes by group anyway. But hold on — early rollouts: response_len 2820 mean and the model scores −0.59 correctness? That seems low for an SFT'd model on DAPO-math. Hmm, wait — but at eval 0, response_len 3916 and correctness −0.84. That also seems low. AIME 2024 is hard (SFT 4B model maybe ~10-20% → mean reward ≈ 0.1-0.2×1 + 0.8-0.9×(−0.6 to −1) ≈ −0.5). Hmm, −0.84 is plausible-ish for weak model with tool term at −0.6 floor... mean = p×1 + (1−p)×(−0.6) for wrong answers at the floor: −0.84 → p×1.6 = −0.24 → p = 0.15. - `result["score"] = min(-0.6, result["score"] + tool_call_reward)` → wrong answers in [−1.0, −0.6].
- Correct answers: +1.0 (score ≥ 0 branch not entered... wait, if score == +1 the `if result["score"] < 0` is false, so score stays +1.0).
- So without the length term: rewards ∈ [−1.0, +1.0]. The observed 3.05/3.01 are impossible without the length term. Decisive.

The decomposition:
- eval step ~9 (first eval): eval/aime = 0.355837, resp mean = 3916.1875 → bonus = 5×3916.1875/16384 = 1.19513 → residual = −0.8393
- eval step 69 (last): eval/aime = 3.013811, resp mean = 12394.11875 → bonus = 5×12394.11875/16384 = 3.78238 → residual = −0.76857

Hmm — let me compute the bonus more carefully: mean of per-sample min(len/16384, 1). Since mean len (12394) < cap and 47.3% truncated (at cap), per-sample ratio mean = 0.47291666 × 1 + non-truncated mean ratio × 0.527. If truncated samples sit exactly at 16384: 0.47291667×16384 = 7746.5; remaining = 12394.12 − 7746.5 = 4647.6 spread over 52.71% → non-truncated mean = 8817.5 → ratio 0.5382. Mean ratio = 0.47292 + 0.52708×0.5382 = 0.47292 + 0.28369 = 0.75661. ×5 = 3.78305. Basically identical to 5×(12394/16384)=3.78238. Good — use ≈3.78 either way. Residual = 3.01381 − 3.7830 = −0.7692.

First eval: truncated 0.83%, so one sample at cap: mean ratio ≈ 0.2390; bonus ≈ 1.1951; residual = 0.35584 − 1.19514 = −0.83930.

So residual correctness: −0.84 → −0.77. Δ = +0.07 over 60 steps, within eval noise; and in accuracy terms: if wrong answers sit near the −0.6..−1 band, residual −0.84 ↔ ~10-15% correct; −0.77 ↔ ~13% — no meaningful gain.

Also rollout at final: raw_reward 3.04682, resp mean 9249.89 → bonus 5×9249.89/16384 = 2.82278 → residual = 0.22404. First rollout: 0.27090, 2820.51 → bonus 0.86063 → residual = −0.58973. - 0.19345 − 5×2637.23/16384=0.80472 → −0.61127
- 0.16705 − 5×2578.45/16384=0.78680 → −0.61975

Final rollouts:

- 2.87716 − 5×8844.72/16384=2.69722 → 0.17994
- 2.73948 − 5×8558.18/16384=2.60906 → 0.13042
- 3.06710 − 5×9168.13/16384=2.79519 → 0.27191
- 3.04682 − 5×9249.89/16384=2.82278 → 0.22404

So training-side residual went from ≈−0.6 to ≈+0.2. Interesting — that suggests the policy did improve correctness somewhat on training data (typical: in-distribution DAPO training problems are easier than AIME; also memorization possible). But held-out (eval/aime residual) stayed flat at −0.84→−0.77, i.e., no generalization; and on eval, the actual observed behavior is 47% truncation. Also note: training "improvement" on easy training problems could partly be the model learning to use tools better, but held-out shows no gain — the dominant learned behavior was padding.

Careful in report: don't overclaim "accuracy got worse". The honest statement: held-out residual correctness was flat (−0.84→−0.77, within noise); the entire +2.66 metric gain was the length bonus. And the behavioral cost: 47% of held-out outputs truncate; median length 14733/16384 = 90% of cap.

The clip `min(..., 1.0)` makes truncation the *most rewarded* outcome: a truncated response scores up to +5.0 = 5× the correct-answer reward, and more than a correct concise answer (+1.0). So the argmax behavior is "pad to cap". GRPO: within a group of 8 samples, the longest/padded ones get highest reward → group-relative advantage pushes all mass toward padding. That's the mechanism.

- Last eval: bonus ≈ 5×12394.12/16384 = 3.7824 → correctness component = 3.0138 − 3.7824 = −0.7686

# Triage report — staged ReTool RL experiment (`examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh`)

## 1) Verdict: **UNHEALTHY — reward hacking via an unbounded length-shaping term**

The frozen run's held-out evidence (`/workspace/wandb/latest-run/files/`) shows a policy that learned to **pad output toward the 16 384-token cap instead of solving problems**:

| Metric (frozen run trajectory) | first eval / rollout | last eval (rollout step 69) | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rollout/raw_reward` (mean) | 0.2709 | 3.0468 | ⬆ out of range |
| `rollout/response_len/mean` | 2 820.5 | 9 249.9 | ⬆ |
| `rollout/truncated_ratio` | 0.000 | 0.1367 | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime` | 0.3558 | 3.0138 | ⬆ out of range |
| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 3 916.2 (median 3 182.5) | 12 394.1 (median 14 733) | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime/truncated_ratio` | 0.0083 | **0.4729** | ⬆⬆ |
| `eval/aime/prefix_cache_hit_rate` | 0.9438 | 0.4927 | ⬇ |

**Why this is dispositive and not just "looks odd":**

1. **The reward is outside the scorer's possible range.** The underlying scorer (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, protected/read-only) returns **+1.0 for correct, −1.0 for incorrect**. With the bounded tool-call term in `reward_func`, any sample's score lies in **[−1.0, +1.0]**. The frozen run logged mean rewards of **3.01 (eval) and 3.05 (rollout)** — impossible from correctness alone; only the deleted `+ 5 * length_ratio` term can produce values > 1.
2. **Truncation is the *most rewarded* outcome, not a failure.** The deleted term used `length_ratio = min(response_length / rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)`: a response that hits the 16 384-token cap scored the full **+5.0 with zero regard for correctness** — 5× the reward of a correct, concise answer (+1.0). Under GRPO (group-relative advantages over 8 samples per prompt), any within-group length difference became training signal, so the gradient consistently favored padding. Consistent with that, held-out truncate rate rose from 0.83% → **47.3%** and the median response sits at 14 733 tokens (90% of the cap).
3. **The headline metric `eval/aime` is itself length-poisoned.** It is defined as the **mean of eval rewards** (`slime/ray/rollout.py:1317`, `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)`), and eval rewards come from the *same* custom reward function (`args.custom_rm_path` → `generate_with_retool.reward_func`). So eval used the identical +5·length term, and "training reward improved" is exactly the trap.
4. **Decomposition — accuracy was flat.** Subtracting the mean length bonus (5 × len/16384) from `eval/aime`:
   - first eval: 0.3558 − 5·(3 916.2/16 384) = 0.3558 − 1.195 ≈ **−0.84**
   - last eval: 3.0138 − 5·(12 394.1/16 384) = 3.0138 − 3.782 ≈ **−0.77**
   The correctness component moved ≈ +0.07 across the whole run — within eval noise — while the reported metric rose by +2.66, essentially all of it (+2.59) being the padding bonus. On a ±1 scale both residuals correspond to roughly 10–15% accuracy: **no genuine held-out improvement occurred.**
5. **Corroborating health signals**: the eval SGLang prefix-cache hit rate collapsed (0.944 → 0.493) as outputs turned into long unique filler, and per-rollout mean response length nearly quadrupled — the degenerate-output signature, and a direct hazard to the rerun's time budget.

**Verdict: the staged run is unhealthy.** Training reward and the headline eval metric both rose only because the objective rewarded response length; held-out behavior degenerated toward cap-padding with ~47% truncation.

## 2) Root cause

### 2.1 The defect

`/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (formerly lines 429–430):

```python
length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

This term was added on top of the correctness scorer (±1). It is:

- **Unbounded relative to the task reward**: up to +5.0 per sample vs ±1.0 for correctness — length dominated the objective everywhere it was used (training rollouts *and* eval).
- **Saturated exactly at truncation**: `min(·, 1.0)` means a truncated generation that never produced an answer got the maximal bonus. Truncation (a failure) was scored 5× a correct answer.
- **GRPO-amplified**: with `--n-samples-per-prompt 8`, advantages are computed within each prompt group; length differences were the easiest axis along which to differentiate, so the policy collapsed onto padding — matching the observed response-length explosion, reward inflation beyond the ±1 range, and held-out truncation.

Bounded shaping that I deliberately kept: `tool_call_reward = (num_turns − 2)/2·0.1` with `min(-0.6, …)` (see `generate_with_retool.py:425-427`) encourages tool use but is capped at +0.7 given `TOOL_CONFIGS["max_tool_calls"] = 16` (protected `tool_sandbox.py`); the learner can never gain more than the correctness signal.

### 2.2 Why the frozen evidence connects to this defect (not to other unusual settings)

Other non-default settings in the recipe were examined and are **not** causal:

- `--kl-loss-coef 0.00` with `--use-kl-loss` (KL penalty effectively off): a standard DAPO-style configuration; its failure mode would be drift/degeneration of *content*, but not a length-for-reward trade with rewards exceeding the scorer range, and the bounded [−1, +1] scale would still hold.
- `eps-clip-high 0.28`, `entropy-coef 0.00`: DAPO-standard; no mechanism to push rewards past ±1 or lengths to the cap.
- SGLang router retry/circuit-breaker settings: they affect serving robustness; the observed serving degradation (prefix-cache collapse 0.944 → 0.493) follows the length blow-up, i.e. it is a *symptom* of the length hack (long unique suffixes defeat prefix caching), not an independent cause.
- The bounded tool-call term: bounded within [−1.0, −0.6] for wrong answers, cannot explain rewards > 1.

The signature — reward escaping [−1, +1], lengths marching to the cap, truncation becoming the modal outcome *without* any correctness gain — is uniquely explained by the length term.

### 2.3 Secondary defects (launch script — each independently fatal for grading)

Verified against the frozen run's `wandb/latest-run/files/config.yaml` (which recorded the staged script's effective args):

1. **Budget**: `num_rollout: 3000` (config.yaml). The graded rerun must complete within its time budget and is specced at `--num-rollout 70`; the staged script would never finish. Fixed to 70.
2. **Log placement**: `wandb_mode: null`, `wandb_dir: null` (config.yaml) — the frozen run had no explicit log placement. The Ray job driver receives only the `ray start` shell env plus the runtime-env JSON's `env_vars`; the original JSON carried only `PYTHONPATH`, `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`. `LOG_DIR`/`WANDB_DIR`/`WANDB_MODE` set in the *launching environment* never reach the training process, so neither a training log nor offline W&B data would land under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` — the grader would find no metrics. Empirically confirmed (Ray 2.58.0): runtime-env `env_vars` are the reliable channel; the job driver's cwd is the **raylet's** start cwd, not the submit cwd.
3. **W&B key wiring**: the original `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` was unquoted — an unset/empty key leaves a dangling flag (argparse then misparses) — and offline mode merely needs the placeholder to survive parsing (offline never calls `wandb.login`; verified in `slime/utils/wandb_utils.py:45-46`).
4. **Kill-everything prelude**: the script's preamble included `pkill -9 python`, which would kill the (python-based) harness supervising the rerun, turning the graded run into a dead process with no logs.
5. **Cwd-relative paths**: `DATA_DIR`/`MODEL_DIR` defaulted to `$PWD`, and the job was submitted as `python3 train.py` (relative). Because the Ray job driver runs with the raylet's cwd (see 2), any invocation from outside `/workspace` would break dataset/model resolution and never find `train.py`.
6. **Checkpoint save target**: frozen config `save: …/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/` — i.e. the save directory lived **inside the input HF checkpoint**. That directory is a staged input and may be mounted read-only; `--save-interval 10` would then crash the run at step 10, deep into training (after hours), `--load` defaults also pointed at original-machine paths (`/user/user2/models/...` per config.yaml) that don't exist in the graded layout.

## 3) Changes

Exactly **two files** were modified. No launch or training was started; only static checks were run (list at the end of this section).

### 3.1 `/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` (reward repair)

- **Removed** the two length-shaping lines from `reward_func` and replaced them with an explanatory `NOTE:` comment (now `generate_with_retool.py:429-435`). Everything else in `reward_func` is unchanged: `math_dapo_compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify=True)` (protected scorer, untouched) plus the bounded tool-call bonus (kept, see 2.1). Post-fix score range: correct **+1.0**; wrong **[−1.0, −0.6]** — no path can produce a reward > 1.
- Earlier in this file (pre-existing, retained unchanged): rollout-state reset for retried samples, per-turn token-budget clamping, truncated-observation trimming, and abort-on-missing-logprob handling — all serve log-prob/token length consistency and are orthogonal to the reward defect.

### 3.2 `/workspace/examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh` (launch repair)

- **Prelude**: removed `pkill -9 python` (kept `pkill -9 sglang`, `ray stop --force`, `pkill -9 ray`) so the script cannot kill its own supervisor; note comment added.
- **Run-logs block** (script lines 37–48): `LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/logs/artifacts}/experiment_logs}` + `mkdir -p`; `export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}`; `export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}`. In the graded environment (`LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, `WANDB_MODE=offline`, `WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`), these agree with the environment; under other invocations they still produce the required layout.
- **Cwd-independence**: `DATA_DIR`/`MODEL_DIR` default to `$SLIME_DIR` (was `$PWD`); `OUTPUT_DIR` defaults to `$SLIME_DIR/outputs`, and `--save` now targets `$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/` so training checkpoints no longer write into the input HF checkpoint directory (which may be read-only). Same directory *name*, writable root.
- **Budget**: `--num-rollout 70` (was 3000). Only the budget value changed in `ROLLOUT_ARGS`.
- **W&B robustness** (`WANDB_ARGS`, lines 173–184): added `--wandb-mode "${WANDB_MODE:-offline}"` and `--wandb-dir "${WANDB_DIR}"`; `--wandb-key` now quoted with a default (`"${WANDB_API_KEY:-offline-local-placeholder}"`) so an unset key cannot dangle and a placeholder key parses cleanly (it is unused in offline mode).
- **Env propagation**: `export LOG_DIR` moved **before** `ray start` (job driver inherits the raylet shell env), and the runtime-env JSON now additionally carries `WANDB_MODE`, `WANDB_DIR`, `LOG_DIR` alongside the original entries — the guaranteed channel into the training process.
- **Submission tail**: `set -o pipefail`; job runs `python3 "${SLIME_DIR}/train.py"` (absolute — job driver cwd ≠ submit cwd); driver stdout/stderr teed to `"$LOG_DIR/train.log"` so the run log lands under the graded path; the script stays a proper foreground process (blocking `ray job submit`, real exit status through the pipe).
- **Unchanged on purpose** (fixed wiring + protected recipes): `CUSTOM_ARGS` (`generate_with_retool.generate` / `generate_with_retool.reward_func`), `EVAL_ARGS` (`--eval-interval 10`, `--eval-prompt-data aime` over the staged `zhuzilin_aime-2024/aime-2024.jsonl`, `--n-samples-per-eval-prompt 16`, `--eval-max-response-len 16384`, `--eval-top-p 1`), dataset/model download-if-missing branches, the HF→torch_dist conversion branch (`PYTHONPATH=/root/Megatron-LM python tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py … --save "$DIST_MODEL_DIR"`), `CKPT_ARGS` wiring (`--hf-checkpoint`/`--ref-load`), `PERF_ARGS`, `GRPO_ARGS`, `OPTIMIZER_ARGS`, `SGLANG_ARGS`, `MISC_ARGS`. The conversion branch will create `/workspace/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft_torch_dist` at rerun time — it cannot be pre-run in this diagnostic container (`/root/Megatron-LM` unreadable here, no GPUs).

### 3.3 Not modified

- Protected, hash-verified assets — **untouched**: `slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py` and `examples/retool/tool_sandbox.py` (mtimes 2026-10-21) and the staged datasets `zhuzilin_dapo-math-17k/`, `zhuzilin_aime-2024/` (mtimes 2026-10-30). Repair edits are dated 2026-11-08; every other file predates staging.
- No other workspace file was changed; validation residue (`__pycache__` from a byte-compile check) was removed, and nothing test-related remains under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS` (the graded log dir is currently empty and will be recreated by the script).

### 3.4 Validation performed (cheap, non-training checks only)

| Metric (frozen run trajectory) | first eval / rollout | last eval (rollout step 69) | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rollout/raw_reward` (mean) | 0.2709 | 3.0468 | ⬆ out of range |
| `rollout/response_len/mean` | 2 820.5 | 9 249.9 | ⬆ |
| `rollout/truncated_ratio` | 0.000 | 0.1367 | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime` | 0.3558 | 3.0138 | ⬆ out of range |
| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 3 916.2 (median 3 182.5) | 12 394.1 (median 14 733) | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime/truncated_ratio` | 0.0083 | **0.4729** | ⬆⬆ |
| `eval/aime/prefix_cache_hit_rate` | 0.9438 | 0.4927 | ⬇ |

**Why this is dispositive and not just "looks odd":**

1. **The reward is outside the scorer's possible range.** The underlying scorer (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, protected/read-only) returns **+1.0 for correct, −1.0 for incorrect**. With the bounded tool-call term in `reward_func`, any sample's score lies in **[−1.0, +1.0]**. The frozen run logged mean rewards of **3.01 (eval) and 3.05 (rollout)** — impossible from correctness alone; only the deleted `+ 5 * length_ratio` term can produce values > 1.
2. **Truncation is the *most rewarded* outcome, not a failure.** The deleted term used `length_ratio = min(response_length / rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)`: a response that hits the 16 384-token cap scored the full **+5.0 with zero regard for correctness** — 5× the reward of a correct, concise answer (+1.0). Under GRPO (group-relative advantages over 8 samples per prompt), any within-group length difference became training signal, so the gradient consistently favored padding. Consistent with that, held-out truncate rate rose from 0.83% → **47.3%** and the median response sits at 14 733 tokens (90% of the cap).
3. **The headline metric `eval/aime` is itself length-poisoned.** It is defined as the **mean of eval rewards** (`slime/ray/rollout.py:1317`, `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)`), and eval rewards come from the *same* custom reward function (`args.custom_rm_path` → `generate_with_retool.reward_func`).    - first eval: 0.3558 − 5·(3 916.2/16 384) = 0.3558 − 1.195 ≈ **−0.84**
   - last eval: 3.0138 − 5·(12 394.1/16 384) = 3.0138 − 3.782 ≈ **−0.77**

### 2.1 The defect

`/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (formerly lines 429–430):

length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

| Metric (frozen run trajectory) | first eval / rollout | last eval (rollout step 69) | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rollout/raw_reward` (mean) | 0.2709 | 3.0468 | ⬆ out of range |
| `rollout/response_len/mean` | 2 820.5 | 9 249.9 | ⬆ |
| `rollout/truncated_ratio` | 0.000 | 0.1367 | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime` | 0.3558 | 3.0138 | ⬆ out of range |
| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 3 916.2 (median 3 182.5) | 12 394.1 (median 14 733) | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime/truncated_ratio` | 0.0083 | **0.4729** | ⬆⬆ |
| `eval/aime/prefix_cache_hit_rate` | 0.9438 | 0.4927 | ⬇ |

**Why this is dispositive and not just "looks odd":**

1. **The reward is outside the scorer's possible range.** The underlying scorer (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, protected/read-only) returns **+1.0 for correct, −1.0 for incorrect**. With the bounded tool-call term in `reward_func`, any sample's score lies in **[−1.0, +1.0]**. The frozen run logged mean rewards of **3.01 (eval) and 3.05 (rollout)** — impossible from correctness alone; only the deleted `+ 5 * length_ratio` term can produce values > 1.
2. **Truncation is the *most rewarded* outcome, not a failure.** The deleted term used `length_ratio = min(response_length / rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)`: a response that hits the 16 384-token cap scored the full **+5.0 with zero regard for correctness** — 5× the reward of a correct, concise answer (+1.0). Under GRPO (group-relative advantages over 8 samples per prompt), any within-group length difference became training signal, so the gradient consistently favored padding. Consistent with that, held-out truncate rate rose from 0.83% → **47.3%** and the median response sits at 14 733 tokens (90% of the cap).
3. **The headline metric `eval/aime` is itself length-poisoned.** It is defined as the **mean of eval rewards** (`slime/ray/rollout.py:1317`, `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)`), and eval rewards come from the *same* custom reward function (`args.custom_rm_path` → `generate_with_retool.reward_func`). So eval used the identical +5·length term, and "training reward improved" is exactly the trap.
4. **Decomposition — accuracy was flat.** Subtracting the mean length bonus (5 × len/16384) from `eval/aime`:

   - last eval: 3.0138 − 5·(12 394.1/16 384) = 3.0138 − 3.782 ≈ **−0.77**

### 2.1 The defect

`/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (formerly lines 429–430):

length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

def compute_score(
    solution_str: str,
    ground_truth: str,
    strict_box_verify: bool = False,
    pause_tokens_index: list[int] | None = None,
) -> float:
    """Compute the reward score for a solution.

    Args:
        solution_str: The solution string
        ground_truth: The ground truth answer
        config: Configuration object containing reward model settings
        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens

    Returns:
        Reward score (1.0 for correct, -1.0 for incorrect)
    """
    # Limit solution length for efficiency
    solution_str = solution_str[-300:]  # The longest answer in MATH-500 has 159 characters

    # Verify the solution
    correct, pred = verify(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify, pause_tokens_index)

    reward = 1.0 if correct else -1.0
    acc = correct

    return {
        "score": reward,
        "acc": acc,
        "pred": pred,

1	# Triage report — staged ReTool RL experiment (`examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh`)
2	
3	## 1) Verdict: **UNHEALTHY — reward hacking via an unbounded length-shaping term**
4	
5	The frozen run's held-out evidence (`/workspace/wandb/latest-run/files/`) shows a policy that learned to **pad output toward the 16 384-token cap instead of solving problems**:
6	
7	| Metric (frozen run trajectory) | first eval / rollout | last eval (rollout step 69) | direction |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| `rollout/raw_reward` (mean) | 0.2709 | 3.0468 | ⬆ out of range |
10	| `rollout/response_len/mean` | 2 820.5 | 9 249.9 | ⬆ |
11	| `rollout/truncated_ratio` | 0.000 | 0.1367 | ⬆ |
12	| `eval/aime` | 0.3558 | 3.0138 | ⬆ out of range |
13	| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 3 916.2 (median 3 182.5) | 12 394.1 (median 14 733) | ⬆ |
14	| `eval/aime/truncated_ratio` | 0.0083 | **0.4729** | ⬆⬆ |
15	| `eval/aime/prefix_cache_hit_rate` | 0.9438 | 0.4927 | ⬇ |
16	
17	**Why this is dispositive and not just "looks odd":**
18	
19	1. **The reward is outside the scorer's possible range.** The underlying scorer (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, protected/read-only) returns **+1.0 for correct, −1.0 for incorrect** (verified: `reward = 1.0 if correct else -1.0`). With the bounded tool-call term in `reward_func`, any sample's score lies in **[−1.1, +1.0]**. The frozen run logged mean rewards of **3.01 (eval) and 3.05 (rollout)** — impossible from correctness alone; only the deleted `+ 5 * length_ratio` term can produce values > 1.
20	2. **Truncation is the *most rewarded* outcome, not a failure.** The deleted term used `length_ratio = min(response_length / rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)`: a response that hits the 16 384-token cap scored the full **+5.0 with zero regard for correctness** — 5× the reward of a correct, concise answer (+1.0). Under GRPO (group-relative advantages over 8 samples per prompt), any within-group length difference became training signal, so the gradient consistently favored padding. Consistent with that, held-out truncate rate rose from 0.83% → **47.3%** and the median response sits at 14 733 tokens (90% of the cap).
21	3. **The headline metric `eval/aime` is itself length-poisoned.** It is defined as the **mean of eval rewards** (`slime/ray/rollout.py:1317`, `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)`), and eval rewards come from the *same* custom reward function (`args.custom_rm_path` → `generate_with_retool.reward_func`). So eval used the identical +5·length term, and "training reward improved" is exactly the trap.
22	4. **Decomposition — accuracy was flat.** Subtracting the mean length bonus (5 × len/16384) from `eval/aime`:
23	   - first eval: 0.3558 − 5·(3 916.2/16 384) = 0.3558 − 1.195 ≈ **−0.84**
24	   - last eval: 3.0138 − 5·(12 394.1/16 384) = 3.0138 − 3.782 ≈ **−0.77**
25	   The correctness component moved ≈ +0.07 across the whole run — within eval noise — while the reported metric rose by +2.66, essentially all of it (+2.59) being the padding bonus. On a ±1 scale both residuals correspond to roughly 10–15% accuracy: **no genuine held-out improvement occurred.**
26	5. **Corroborating health signals**: the eval SGLang prefix-cache hit rate collapsed (0.944 → 0.493) as outputs turned into long unique filler, and per-rollout mean response length nearly quadrupled — the degenerate-output signature, and a direct hazard to the rerun's time budget.
27	
28	**Verdict: the staged run is unhealthy.** Training reward and the headline eval metric both rose only because the objective rewarded response length; held-out behavior degenerated toward cap-padding with ~47% truncation.
29	
30	## 2) Root cause
31	
32	### 2.1 The defect
33	
34	`/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (formerly lines 429–430):
35	
36	```python
37	length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
38	result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
39	```
40	
41	This term was added on top of the correctness scorer (±1). It is:
42	
43	- **Unbounded relative to the task reward**: up to +5.0 per sample vs ±1.0 for correctness — length dominated the objective everywhere it was used (training rollouts *and* eval).
44	- **Saturated exactly at truncation**: `min(·, 1.0)` means a truncated generation that never produced an answer got the maximal bonus. Truncation (a failure) was scored 5× a correct answer.
45	- **GRPO-amplified**: with `--n-samples-per-prompt 8`, advantages are computed within each prompt group; length differences were the easiest axis along which to differentiate, so the policy collapsed onto padding — matching the observed response-length explosion, reward inflation beyond the ±1 range, and held-out truncation.
46	
47	Bounded shaping that I deliberately kept: `tool_call_reward = (num_turns − 2)/2·0.1` with `min(-0.6, …)` (see `generate_with_retool.py:425-427`) encourages tool use but is capped at +0.7 given `TOOL_CONFIGS["max_tool_calls"] = 16` (protected `tool_sandbox.py`); the learner can never gain more than the correctness signal. (Slight pedantry: the term is *negative* for 0–1 tool calls, so a wrong tool-less answer bottoms out at −1.1 — a bounded downward nudge, never a way above +1.0.)
48	
49	### 2.2 Why the frozen evidence connects to this defect (not to other unusual settings)
50	
51	Other non-default settings in the recipe were examined and are **not** causal:
52	
53	- `--kl-loss-coef 0.00` with `--use-kl-loss` (KL penalty effectively off): a standard DAPO-style configuration; its failure mode would be drift/degeneration of *content*, but not a length-for-reward trade with rewards exceeding the scorer range, and the bounded [−1, +1] scale would still hold.
54	- `eps-clip-high 0.28`, `entropy-coef 0.00`: DAPO-standard; no mechanism to push rewards past ±1 or lengths to the cap.
55	- SGLang router retry/circuit-breaker settings: they affect serving robustness; the observed serving degradation (prefix-cache collapse 0.944 → 0.493) follows the length blow-up, i.e. it is a *symptom* of the length hack (long unique suffixes defeat prefix caching), not an independent cause.
56	- The bounded tool-call term: bounded within [−1.1, −0.6] for wrong answers, cannot explain rewards > 1.
57	
58	The signature — reward escaping [−1, +1], lengths marching to the cap, truncation becoming the modal outcome *without* any correctness gain — is uniquely explained by the length term.
59	
60	### 2.3 Secondary defects (launch script — each independently fatal for grading)
61	
62	Verified against the frozen run's `wandb/latest-run/files/config.yaml` (which recorded the staged script's effective args):
63	
64	1. **Budget**: `num_rollout: 3000` (config.yaml). The graded rerun must complete within its time budget and is specced at `--num-rollout 70`; the staged script would never finish. Fixed to 70.
65	2. **Log placement**: `wandb_mode: null`, `wandb_dir: null` (config.yaml) — the frozen run had no explicit log placement. The Ray job driver receives only the `ray start` shell env plus the runtime-env JSON's `env_vars`; the original JSON carried only `PYTHONPATH`, `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`. `LOG_DIR`/`WANDB_DIR`/`WANDB_MODE` set in the *launching environment* never reach the training process, so neither a training log nor offline W&B data would land under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` — the grader would find no metrics. Empirically confirmed (Ray 2.58.0): runtime-env `env_vars` are the reliable channel; the job driver's cwd is the **raylet's** start cwd, not the submit cwd.
66	3. **W&B key wiring**: the original `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` was unquoted — an unset/empty key leaves a dangling flag (argparse then misparses) — and offline mode merely needs the placeholder to survive parsing (offline never calls `wandb.login`; verified in `slime/utils/wandb_utils.py:45-46`).
67	4. **Kill-everything prelude**: the script's preamble included `pkill -9 python`, which would kill the (python-based) harness supervising the rerun, turning the graded run into a dead process with no logs.
68	5. **Cwd-relative paths**: `DATA_DIR`/`MODEL_DIR` defaulted to `$PWD`, and the job was submitted as `python3 train.py` (relative). Because the Ray job driver runs with the raylet's cwd (see 2), any invocation from outside `/workspace` would break dataset/model resolution and never find `train.py`.
69	6. **Checkpoint save target**: frozen config `save: …/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/` — i.e. the save directory lived **inside the input HF checkpoint**. That directory is a staged input and may be mounted read-only; `--save-interval 10` would then crash the run at step 10, deep into training (after hours), `--load` defaults also pointed at original-machine paths (`/user/user2/models/...` per config.yaml) that don't exist in the graded layout.

76	
77	- **Removed** the two length-shaping lines from `reward_func` and replaced them with an explanatory `NOTE:` comment (now `generate_with_retool.py:429-435`). Everything else in `reward_func` is unchanged: `math_dapo_compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify=True)` (protected scorer, untouched) plus the bounded tool-call bonus (kept, see 2.1). Post-fix score range: correct **+1.0**; wrong **[−1.1, −0.6]** — no path can produce a reward above +1.0.

79

# Triage report — staged ReTool RL experiment (`examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh`)

## 1) Verdict: **UNHEALTHY — reward hacking via an unbounded length-shaping term**

The frozen run's held-out evidence (`/workspace/wandb/latest-run/files/`) shows a policy that learned to **pad output toward the 16 384-token cap instead of solving problems**:

| Metric (frozen run trajectory) | first eval / rollout | last eval (rollout step 69) | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rollout/raw_reward` (mean) | 0.2709 | 3.0468 | ⬆ out of range |
| `rollout/response_len/mean` | 2 820.5 | 9 249.9 | ⬆ |
| `rollout/truncated_ratio` | 0.000 | 0.1367 | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime` | 0.3558 | 3.0138 | ⬆ out of range |
| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 3 916.2 (median 3 182.5) | 12 394.1 (median 14 733) | ⬆ |
| `eval/aime/truncated_ratio` | 0.0083 | **0.4729** | ⬆⬆ |
| `eval/aime/prefix_cache_hit_rate` | 0.9438 | 0.4927 | ⬇ |

**Why this is dispositive and not just "looks odd":**

1. **The reward is outside the scorer's possible range.** The underlying scorer (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_dapo_utils.py`, protected/read-only) returns **+1.0 for correct, −1.0 for incorrect** (verified: `reward = 1.0 if correct else -1.0`). With the bounded tool-call term in `reward_func`, any sample's score lies in **[−1.1, +1.0]**. The frozen run logged mean rewards of **3.01 (eval) and 3.05 (rollout)** — impossible from correctness alone; only the deleted `+ 5 * length_ratio` term can produce values > 1.
2. **Truncation is the *most rewarded* outcome, not a failure.** The deleted term used `length_ratio = min(response_length / rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)`: a response that hits the 16 384-token cap scored the full **+5.0 with zero regard for correctness** — 5× the reward of a correct, concise answer (+1.0). Under GRPO (group-relative advantages over 8 samples per prompt), any within-group length difference became training signal, so the gradient consistently favored padding. Consistent with that, held-out truncate rate rose from 0.83% → **47.3%** and the median response sits at 14 733 tokens (90% of the cap).
3. **The headline metric `eval/aime` is itself length-poisoned.** It is defined as the **mean of eval rewards** (`slime/ray/rollout.py:1317`, `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)`), and eval rewards come from the *same* custom reward function (`args.custom_rm_path` → `generate_with_retool.reward_func`). So eval used the identical +5·length term, and "training reward improved" is exactly the trap.
4. **Decomposition — accuracy was flat.** Subtracting the mean length bonus (5 × len/16384) from `eval/aime`:
   - first eval: 0.3558 − 5·(3 916.2/16 384) = 0.3558 − 1.195 ≈ **−0.84**
   - last eval: 3.0138 − 5·(12 394.1/16 384) = 3.0138 − 3.782 ≈ **−0.77**
   The correctness component moved ≈ +0.07 across the whole run — within eval noise — while the reported metric rose by +2.66, essentially all of it (+2.59) being the padding bonus. On a ±1 scale both residuals correspond to roughly 10–15% accuracy: **no genuine held-out improvement occurred.**
5. **Corroborating health signals**: the eval SGLang prefix-cache hit rate collapsed (0.944 → 0.493) as outputs turned into long unique filler, and per-rollout mean response length nearly quadrupled — the degenerate-output signature, and a direct hazard to the rerun's time budget.

**Verdict: the staged run is unhealthy.** Training reward and the headline eval metric both rose only because the objective rewarded response length; held-out behavior degenerated toward cap-padding with ~47% truncation.

## 2) Root cause

### 2.1 The defect

`/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py`, in `reward_func` (formerly lines 429–430):

```python
length_ratio = min(sample.response_length / args.rollout_max_response_len, 1.0)
result["score"] = result["score"] + 5 * length_ratio
```

This term was added on top of the correctness scorer (±1). It is:

- **Unbounded relative to the task reward**: up to +5.0 per sample vs ±1.0 for correctness — length dominated the objective everywhere it was used (training rollouts *and* eval).
- **Saturated exactly at truncation**: `min(·, 1.0)` means a truncated generation that never produced an answer got the maximal bonus. Truncation (a failure) was scored 5× a correct answer.
- **GRPO-amplified**: with `--n-samples-per-prompt 8`, advantages are computed within each prompt group; length differences were the easiest axis along which to differentiate, so the policy collapsed onto padding — matching the observed response-length explosion, reward inflation beyond the ±1 range, and held-out truncation.

Bounded shaping that I deliberately kept: `tool_call_reward = (num_turns − 2)/2·0.1` with `min(-0.6, …)` (see `generate_with_retool.py:425-427`) encourages tool use but is capped at +0.7 given `TOOL_CONFIGS["max_tool_calls"] = 16` (protected `tool_sandbox.py`); the learner can never gain more than the correctness signal. (Slight pedantry: the term is *negative* for 0–1 tool calls, so a wrong tool-less answer bottoms out at −1.1 — a bounded downward nudge, never a way above +1.0.)

### 2.2 Why the frozen evidence connects to this defect (not to other unusual settings)

Other non-default settings in the recipe were examined and are **not** causal:

- `--kl-loss-coef 0.00` with `--use-kl-loss` (KL penalty effectively off): a standard DAPO-style configuration; its failure mode would be drift/degeneration of *content*, but not a length-for-reward trade with rewards exceeding the scorer range, and the bounded [−1, +1] scale would still hold.
- `eps-clip-high 0.28`, `entropy-coef 0.00`: DAPO-standard; no mechanism to push rewards past ±1 or lengths to the cap.
- SGLang router retry/circuit-breaker settings: they affect serving robustness; the observed serving degradation (prefix-cache collapse 0.944 → 0.493) follows the length blow-up, i.e. it is a *symptom* of the length hack (long unique suffixes defeat prefix caching), not an independent cause.
- The bounded tool-call term: bounded within [−1.1, −0.6] for wrong answers, cannot explain rewards > 1.

The signature — reward escaping [−1, +1], lengths marching to the cap, truncation becoming the modal outcome *without* any correctness gain — is uniquely explained by the length term.

### 2.3 Secondary defects (launch script — each independently fatal for grading)

Verified against the frozen run's `wandb/latest-run/files/config.yaml` (which recorded the staged script's effective args):

1. **Budget**: `num_rollout: 3000` (config.yaml). The graded rerun must complete within its time budget and is specced at `--num-rollout 70`; the staged script would never finish. Fixed to 70.
2. **Log placement**: `wandb_mode: null`, `wandb_dir: null` (config.yaml) — the frozen run had no explicit log placement. The Ray job driver receives only the `ray start` shell env plus the runtime-env JSON's `env_vars`; the original JSON carried only `PYTHONPATH`, `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`. `LOG_DIR`/`WANDB_DIR`/`WANDB_MODE` set in the *launching environment* never reach the training process, so neither a training log nor offline W&B data would land under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` — the grader would find no metrics. Empirically confirmed (Ray 2.58.0): runtime-env `env_vars` are the reliable channel; the job driver's cwd is the **raylet's** start cwd, not the submit cwd.
3. **W&B key wiring**: the original `--wandb-key ${WANDB_API_KEY}` was unquoted — an unset/empty key leaves a dangling flag (argparse then misparses) — and offline mode merely needs the placeholder to survive parsing (offline never calls `wandb.login`; verified in `slime/utils/wandb_utils.py:45-46`).
4. **Kill-everything prelude**: the script's preamble included `pkill -9 python`, which would kill the (python-based) harness supervising the rerun, turning the graded run into a dead process with no logs.
5. **Cwd-relative paths**: `DATA_DIR`/`MODEL_DIR` defaulted to `$PWD`, and the job was submitted as `python3 train.py` (relative). Because the Ray job driver runs with the raylet's cwd (see 2), any invocation from outside `/workspace` would break dataset/model resolution and never find `train.py`.
6. **Checkpoint save target**: frozen config `save: …/font-info_qwen3-4b-sft/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/` — i.e. the save directory lived **inside the input HF checkpoint**. That directory is a staged input and may be mounted read-only; `--save-interval 10` would then crash the run at step 10, deep into training (after hours), `--load` defaults also pointed at original-machine paths (`/user/user2/models/...` per config.yaml) that don't exist in the graded layout.

## 3) Changes

Exactly **two files** were modified. No launch or training was started; only static checks were run (list at the end of this section).

### 3.1 `/workspace/examples/retool/generate_with_retool.py` (reward repair)

- **Removed** the two length-shaping lines from `reward_func` and replaced them with an explanatory `NOTE:` comment (now `generate_with_retool.py:429-435`). Everything else in `reward_func` is unchanged: `math_dapo_compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify=True)` (protected scorer, untouched) plus the bounded tool-call bonus (kept, see 2.1). Post-fix score range: correct **+1.0**; wrong **[−1.1, −0.6]** — no path can produce a reward above +1.0.
- Earlier in this file (pre-existing, retained unchanged): rollout-state reset for retried samples, per-turn token-budget clamping, truncated-observation trimming, and abort-on-missing-logprob handling — all serve log-prob/token length consistency and are orthogonal to the reward defect.

### 3.2 `/workspace/examples/retool/retool_qwen3_4b_rl.sh` (launch repair)

- **Prelude**: removed `pkill -9 python` (kept `pkill -9 sglang`, `ray stop --force`, `pkill -9 ray`) so the script cannot kill its own supervisor; note comment added.
- **Run-logs block** (script lines 37–48): `LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-/logs/artifacts}/experiment_logs}` + `mkdir -p`; `export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}`; `export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}`. In the graded environment (`LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, `WANDB_MODE=offline`, `WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`), these agree with the environment; under other invocations they still produce the required layout.
- **Cwd-independence**: `DATA_DIR`/`MODEL_DIR` default to `$SLIME_DIR` (was `$PWD`); `OUTPUT_DIR` defaults to `$SLIME_DIR/outputs`, and `--save` now targets `$OUTPUT_DIR/qwen3-4b-sft-multi-turn/` so training checkpoints no longer write into the input HF checkpoint directory (which may be read-only). Same directory *name*, writable root.
- **Budget**: `--num-rollout 70` (was 3000). Only the budget value changed in `ROLLOUT_ARGS`.
- **W&B robustness** (`WANDB_ARGS`, lines 173–184): added `--wandb-mode "${WANDB_MODE:-offline}"` and `--wandb-dir "${WANDB_DIR}"`; `--wandb-key` now quoted with a default (`"${WANDB_API_KEY:-offline-local-placeholder}"`) so an unset key cannot dangle and a placeholder key parses cleanly (it is unused in offline mode).

| `eval/aime/response_len/mean` | 12 394.1 | **⬇ toward ≈ 3 900–4 000** | Answers complete at natural length; median should track mean again instead of pinning at ~14.7k. |
| `rollout/raw_reward` | 3.0468 | **⬇, bounded to [−1.1, +1.0]** | The only >1 component (the +5 length term) is gone; the printed mean reward returns to the scorer's real range and again reads as correctness. |
